account: On 10 September 2018 the Green Bank Observatory announced a convolutional neural network found 72 previously undetected pulses from repeating fast radio burst FRB 121102. They were in a five-hour, 400-terabyte Green Bank Telescope observation made on 26 August 2017. Gerry Zhang, a University of California, Berkeley graduate student, built it with Breakthrough Listen collaborators. Conventional algorithms had found 21 bursts in the same data. The combined 93 pulses, including 45 within the first 30 minutes, were reported in a peer-reviewed Astrophysical Journal paper (Zhang et al. 2018). They served to search for periodicity. The detections come from a re-analysis of the team's own data. No independent re-detection by another group was found in the sources.

ai_role.statement: The CNN flagged 72 pulses in data that a classical de-dispersion search had already processed, finding 21. The detections were vetted by the authors and accepted in peer review. The result is a verified discovery, but the wording “independently confirmed” is not met. No re-detection by another group is among the sources.
